chose: render-phase state restore (React's documented adjust-state-during-render pattern) + useHydrated(), not setState-in-useEffect
over: useState+useEffect to restore localStorage filters on mount
because: oxlint's react-hooks/set-state-in-effect flagged the effect-based restore; the repo's own established idiom for browser-only/SSR-mismatch state (use-hydrated.ts, use-mobile.ts, ThisWeekPanel's useHydrated) is useSyncExternalStore + a render-phase state adjustment, which needs no extra committed frame and gives the linter nothing to flag

chose: hasActiveFilters/countSheetFilters still track includeUntimed, but only hasActiveFilters counts it now
over: dropping includeUntimed from hasActiveFilters too since it left the sheet
because: includeUntimed is still a real filter (server-side predicate input) that can differ from its default — Clear filters and the inline Clear-filters affordance must still notice that; only countSheetFilters (the More filters badge) has to stop counting it, since that badge counts what is physically inside the sheet and this checkbox moved to the time dropdown

chose: persist.ts stores a version-tagged, whole-blob-discard-on-mismatch shape with per-field type validation, keyed per household, source excluded
over: a per-field migration ladder, or trusting the stored JSON's shape without type-checking each field
because: the filter set is small enough that resetting to defaults once on a shape change is cheap and far less code than a migration ladder; per-field type checks (not just presence checks) are what make a corrupt/old/hand-edited blob degrade to defaults instead of crashing or silently misapplying a wrong-typed value as a filter
